sections.label: Foreign interference in domestic politics
sections.summary: Foreign interference in domestic politics and electoral processes must always be factored into social and psychological defence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Foreign interference in domestic politics and electoral processes cannot be underestimated and must always be factored into our social and psychological defence.

sections.label: Election laws prohibit foreigners
sections.summary: Election laws expressly prohibit foreigners from taking part in election activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: First, our election laws expressly prohibit foreigners from taking part in election activities.

sections.label: Public Order Act amended
sections.summary: The Public Order Act was amended this year to let Police refuse permits for assemblies organised by or involving foreigners and directed towards political ends.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Beyond elections, the Public Order Act was also amended this year to make clear that the Police may refuse to grant a permit for public assemblies and processions organised by or involving the participation of foreigners or foreign entities and directed towards political ends.

sections.label: Government introducing legislation
sections.summary: Through stakeholder consultations, the Government will introduce legislation with public education and, where appropriate, co-regulation with industry players.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Through consultations with stakeholders, the Government will be introducing legislation, accompanied by public education and, where appropriate, co-regulation with industry players.

sections.label: Foreign interference and social media
sections.summary: The Ministry will not address details publicly, will never let its guard down, and is in conversations with social media organisations like Facebook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Are there actual incidents of foreigners interfering in our electoral system or our electoral process in the past?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The second question is, will the Ministry be working with social media organisations, like Facebook and Google, to help fight fake news?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The details will not be convenient for me to address publicly, but suffice to say that we will never let our guard down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It may be an interference or an attempt to interfere in our electoral process, or it may be an attempt to influence our public opinion or our own local organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second issue about working with social media organisations like Facebook, yes, we do have conversations with them on how we can collectively do this better and it will be one of the stakeholders which we will be consulting closely on the way forward.
